reading.rtitle: Five Habits of a Good Player
paras: Talent is not the whole story. The players who get better are the players with good habits. Here are five habits we see in every good player at this camp.
One: they always sleep eight hours. Two: they usually drink water before, during and after practice -- never soda.
Three: they often eat a small snack one hour before the game. Four: they sometimes rest, and that is not laziness. A tired body doesn't learn.
Five: they never say 'I can't'. They say 'not yet'. Two words, and they change everything.

items: Good players always sleep eight hours.
One: they always sleep eight hours.
Good players usually drink soda during practice.
They usually drink water -- never soda.
Resting is a bad habit for a player.
They sometimes rest, and that is not laziness.
Good players say 'not yet' instead of 'I can't'.
They never say 'I can't'. They say 'not yet'.

listenings.text: Hi, it's Tyler. My coach asks us about our habits every month, so here are mine. I always wake up at six thirty, even on the weekend. I usually have a big breakfast, but I never eat before practice. I often go to the gym with my brother, maybe three times a week. I sometimes play video games until late, and then I am tired the next day. And I never drink soda in the season. Never. That is the only rule I really follow.

Good morning, group two. Before we start, one minute about water. You often forget this, so listen. Drink water before practice, not only after. A big glass, thirty minutes before. During practice, small drinks, many times. And after practice, drink again, even if you are not thirsty. Your body always needs more water than you think, and a tired body never plays well. That's all. Now, court B, in five minutes.

extra_audio.text: Bruno always wakes up early on a school day. He usually has a small breakfast at home. He often goes to the gym after school. He sometimes plays video games until late. He never drinks soda before a game.
